about: Long before “orange wine” was a trend, white grapes in the Republic of Georgia were fermented on their skins, a tradition thousands of years old. Rkatsiteli is the great white grape of that tradition, and Dr. Konstantin Frank, who managed vineyards in Soviet Georgia before emigrating in 1951, was the first to plant it in the Finger Lakes. This amber bottling from the family winery on Keuka Lake is a nod to the grape’s homeland and to the founder who carried it to New York.

The fruit comes from the estate’s Rkatsiteli vines, the oldest planted in 1983. After a mid-May freeze in 2023 cut the crop, the surviving grapes were destemmed and fermented on their skins for about a month in open-top vessels with punchdowns twice a day, then left on the skins for another month. The wine then aged eight months in six barrels of acacia wood, a less common choice than oak, and only 150 cases were made.

The skin contact gives an amber color and a gentle tannic grip unusual in a white wine. The winery describes toasted orange peel, macerated peach, fresh ginger and citrus zest on the nose, a rich palate of ripe peach and apricot with ginger spice, and a long finish of dried fruit. It sits between a white and a red at the table, which makes it an easy match for wood-fired cooking.
facts: Skin-fermented (about 1 month), then 1 more month on skins; twice-daily punchdowns
